wire.headline: Northgate Homes to cut 1,200 jobs amid weak housing demand
sentences: Northgate Homes has announced plans to lay off 1,200 staff members across its sites in the UK.
CEO Marian Holt attributed the decision to weak housing demand in the market.
The company's shares dropped 4.5% in early trading following the announcement.
The layoffs are intended to reduce operating costs by 310m GBP annually.
The company projects a revenue decline of 12% by March 2027.
The broader restructuring plan aims to cut overheads by eliminating 4,800 roles.
The board of directors approved the plan on 4 November after completing a review.

PD.headline: Deeside Faces Closure and Funding Cuts as Mayor Announces Retraining Package

sentences.text: Plans to cut 1,200 staff members across its sites in the UK have been announced by Northgate Homes.
A site in Deeside is scheduled to close by June 2027, a decision that will impact 40 staff members.
Mayor Elara Vance has announced a £5m retraining package to assist those affected by the changes.
Following the announcement, the company's shares fell 4.5% in early trading.
A local school in Deeside is set to lose 15% of its funding, adding to the community's financial concerns.
The community group Deeside Future is demanding job guarantees in response to the impending closures and cuts.

ND.headline: Northgate Cuts Jobs Citing Weak Demand as Unions Warn of Action

sentences.text: CEO Marian Holt attributed the company's recent strategic decision to weak housing demand.
Shares fell 4.5% in early trading following the announcement of the move.
Unite the Union warned that potential industrial action could occur next month.
Analyst Sam Reed from Finch Capital described the move as premature.
Local MP David Clarke demanded an inquiry into the resulting job losses.
The homeowner group SafeStart alleged there had been 18 months of delays.
Northgate was founded in 1988 in Deeside with 50 employees.
The company plans to open 12 new sites in January 2028.
Deputy General Manager Alan Foster denied any quality control failures.
Consultancy PricewaterhouseCoopers is advising on the restructuring costs.
Trade union T&GWU joined Unite in criticizing the project timeline.
Regional developer BuildRight offered to buy 300 plots.
Housing charity Shelter reported that 2,500 homeless families were affected.
